title: Impact of a supportive care Pharmacist Consultation Service (scPCS) on drug therapy safety in oncology patients
summary:
During drug-based tumor therapy, side effects may occur that reduce patients' quality of life and that can make it difficult to continue treatment. Side effects can be treated with additional medications (known as supportive therapy). These are often not used in accordance with existing guidelines, which can compromise drug therapy safety. 
The study examines the influence of pharmacist care on drug therapy safety in outpatient cancer patients. The pharmacists' care includes evidence-based recommendations for supportive therapy to physicians, training for staff, and counseling for patients on how to deal with symptoms and side effects of tumor medication. The effect of these measures on medication safety will be determined by evaluating questionnaires, electronic treatment data, and patient interviews.
conditions: ICD-10-GM C00 - C75 - malignant neoplasms, with the exception of C50 - C68; C80 - malignant neoplasm, without specification of site

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Start of a tumor therapy, intravenous therapy, written medication plan
Exclusion criteria:
Gynecological or urological tumor disease; hematological malignant disease; insufficient knowledge of the German language; pathophysiological cognitive impairments that severely affect memory performance; pregnancy and breastfeeding; Treatment with a drug for the tumor disease that was approved in Germany or the EU after recruitment for the study began.
